You are an implementation worker for the freytag-forge repository at /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. Your current working directory is the repository itself; edit files here directly. Boundary: NO model call, NO network call, never git commit. Edit ONLY the files you own: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/storygame/story_package/situation_trace.py, /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/scripts/situation_trace.py, /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/tests/test_situation_trace.py, /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/tests/shard_durations.json. Do NOT edit story data (/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/data), any other file under storygame/, packages/, other tests, or anything under .plans/. The repo has unrelated uncommitted changes; leave them alone.

GOAL. Turn a read-only prototype into a tested project feature. The prototype is /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.plans/story-data-phase0/render_trace.py (read it first; do not edit it). It prints a "situation trace" for ONE hardcoded case (Reyes demanding a memory card): a generated reading view that starts from a story situation and shows what triggers it, where it leads, and what the next scene needs. Your job is slice 1: a GENERAL version of its data-driven sections 1-3, usable for any anchor in any story package. Do NOT port the prototype's section 4 (response simulation) or section 5 (story gaps) or its 'What the story says, next to what the engine checks' sub-table; those stay in the prototype for now. The output must never contain a plausible-responses table or a gaps section, because it will be given to blind reviewers who must discover those themselves.

DELIVERABLES.
1. /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/storygame/story_package/situation_trace.py: `render_situation_trace(root: Path, anchor: str) -> str`, plus helpers. `root` is a story package directory (e.g. /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/data/stories/continuity-initiative). Load typed data through the existing loader (`storygame.story_package.loader.load_story_package`, models in storygame/story_package/models.py) wherever the models expose the field; read raw YAML only for a field the typed package does not expose. `anchor` is the exact id of exactly one of: a pacing event, an incident, or a transition. Resolve it; if it matches none raise ValueError('unknown anchor ...') naming the id; if it matches more than one kind raise ValueError('ambiguous anchor ...') listing the kinds. The function is pure and deterministic: it never mutates the package, never touches the network, and the same input gives byte-identical output.
2. Output format (Markdown). Title line `# Situation trace: <anchor>`, a line saying it is generated, read-only, edit the sources. Then these sections, with these exact headings:
   `## 1. The situation`, `## 2. Where the situation leads`, `## 3. What the next scene needs`.
   For a PACING EVENT anchor, sections 1-3 must reproduce the prototype's wording and structure for its sections 1, 2 and 3 (see the equality check below), including: the line `- Pacing event `ID` fires at turn N when: <conditions or 'always'>.`, one indented producer line per condition fact (`  - `fact` (purpose) comes from: producer; producer`), `- It sets: ...`, the event's first realization line `- Reyes's line` generalised to `- Line: “<text>”` (the prototype's line starting 'Reyes in the story files:' is dropped), and in section 2 for each effect fact the list of consumers tagged [wording], [gate] or [world] plus the closing sentence `Nothing reads it except a line of wording.` or `It feeds more than wording.`. Section 3 is the exit: the transition(s) whose source scene is the event's scene (if several, one subsection each, ordered by priority then id) with the table `| Needs | Meaning | Produced by |` and the line `It also lists `X` as a required dependency.` (one line per dependency, same wording; omit if none). Reuse the prototype's `producers`/`consumers` logic, generalised to take the loaded story data rather than module-level globals.
   For an INCIDENT anchor: section 1 gives the incident id, scene, each outcome (id, storylet, realization text from its source, advantages, costs), the recovery storylet, the missed-window event and the observation claim ids. Section 2 gives, for each advantage and cost fact, its consumers (same kind tags). Section 3 is the incident's successor transition (as above).
   For a TRANSITION anchor: section 1 gives source and target scene and priority; section 2 lists, for each trigger fact, its consumers other than this transition; section 3 is that transition (as above).
   After the exit table in section 3 add, for every claim that establishes a trigger fact, a short `### What the engine checks to deliver these` table with columns claim id, what it requires (facts), what thing it requires her to be near (reach entities, or the words `names no thing`), and the line `It does not check who holds anything.` ONLY if the claim has no custody requirement in the typed model. Keep statements limited to what the typed model actually says.
3. /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/scripts/situation_trace.py: argparse script, `python scripts/situation_trace.py <anchor> [--root PATH]` (default root /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/data/stories/continuity-initiative), prints the trace to stdout, exit 0; on ValueError prints the message to stderr and exits 2.
4. /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/tests/test_situation_trace.py: pytest tests (style of the neighbouring tests/, player-input guide n/a). Cover: pacing-event anchor `officer_presses_1a`, incident anchor `i_2a_real_leak`, and transition anchor `t_1b_1c` each render all three headings and non-empty content; unknown anchor and (using a small synthetic duplicate-id package built in tmp_path by copying the real story directory and renaming one id so an event and a transition share an id) ambiguous anchor raise ValueError; determinism (two calls identical); the package files are unchanged after rendering (compare file bytes before/after); output contains neither the word 'gaps' as a heading nor a plausible-responses table. Independent expectations only: assert concrete facts you verified by reading the story files (e.g. the officer event's turn number and one of its producers), do not derive expected text from the module under test. No --cov.
5. /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/tests/shard_durations.json: add the new test file with the repo script, exactly: `cd /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge && export TMPDIR=/tmp PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge:/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/packages/worldkeeper/src && /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python scripts/regen_shard_durations.py --missing-only`; the diff of tests/shard_durations.json must be only the added entry.

GENERALITY RULES (checked). /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/storygame/story_package/situation_trace.py must contain no hardcoded story ids or names: no strings such as officer, memory_card, kristin, michelle, laptop, reyes, continuity, 1a, 2a. Everything comes from the loaded package. Stay story-agnostic.

HOW TO RUN (from /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge; never bare python, never uv): `export TMPDIR=/tmp PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge:/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/packages/worldkeeper/src && /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_situation_trace.py tests/test_regen_shard_durations.py -q --no-cov -p no:cacheprovider`. Never use --cov. Then `/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check storygame/story_package/situation_trace.py scripts/situation_trace.py tests/test_situation_trace.py && /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m ruff format storygame/story_package/situation_trace.py scripts/situation_trace.py tests/test_situation_trace.py`. Smoke: `export TMPDIR=/tmp PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge:/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/packages/worldkeeper/src && /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python scripts/situation_trace.py officer_presses_1a`.

EQUALITY CHECK you must satisfy. Run the prototype (`export TMPDIR=/tmp PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge:/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/packages/worldkeeper/src && /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.plans/story-data-phase0/render_trace.py /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge`) and your CLI for `officer_presses_1a`. Take each output from the line `## 1. The situation` up to (not including) the line `### What the story says, next to what the engine checks` in the prototype, and up to (not including) the line `### What the engine checks to deliver these` in yours; delete the single line beginning `- Reyes in the story files:` from the prototype text and change `- Reyes's line: ` to `- Line: ` in it, and rename the heading `## 2. Where the demand leads` to `## 2. Where the situation leads` and `## 3. What Kristin needs to leave 1A` to `## 3. What the next scene needs`, and replace the line `Transition `t_1a_1b` needs all of:` with whatever your module prints for that line generically (a sentence of the form `Transition `ID` needs all of:`). After these listed normalisations the two texts must be identical. If you find the prototype and the spec disagree, follow the prototype's output for section content and stop and write the discrepancy to /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/bench/results/story-data/situation-trace-notes.txt rather than guessing.

for a in officer_presses_1a i_2a_real_leak t_1b_1c pursuit_1b; do

/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python scripts/situation_trace.py no_such_anchor 2>/tmp/st_err.txt; rc=$?
[ $rc -eq 2 ] && grep -qi 'unknown anchor' /tmp/st_err.txt || { echo "FAIL: unknown anchor should exit 2 with 'unknown anchor', got rc=$rc: $(cat /tmp/st_err.txt)"; exit 1; }
/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python scripts/situation_trace.py officer_presses_1a > /tmp/st_b.md; cmp /tmp/st_officer_presses_1a.md /tmp/st_b.md || { echo 'FAIL: nondeterministic output'; exit 1; }
/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.plans/story-data-phase0/render_trace.py /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge > /tmp/st_proto.md || exit 1
python3 - <<'EOF'
import re,sys
def cut(text, start, stop):
    lines = text.splitlines()
    i = next(n for n, l in enumerate(lines) if l.startswith(start))
    j = next(n for n, l in enumerate(lines) if l.startswith(stop))
    return lines[i:j]
p = cut(open('/tmp/st_proto.md').read(), '## 1. The situation', '### What the story says')
g = cut(open('/tmp/st_officer_presses_1a.md').read(), '## 1. The situation', '### What the engine checks to deliver these')
p = [l for l in p if not l.startswith('- Reyes in the story files:')]
p = [l.replace("- Reyes's line: ", '- Line: ').replace('## 2. Where the demand leads', '## 2. Where the situation leads').replace('## 3. What Kristin needs to leave 1A', '## 3. What the next scene needs') for l in p]
p = [re.sub(r'^Transition `[^`]+` needs all of:$', 'Transition NEEDS', l) for l in p]
g = [re.sub(r'^Transition `[^`]+` needs all of:$', 'Transition NEEDS', l) for l in g]
if p != g:
    import difflib
    print('FAIL: sections 1-3 differ from the prototype after normalisation:')
    print('\n'.join(list(difflib.unified_diff(p, g, 'prototype', 'module', lineterm=''))[:60]))
    sys.exit(1)
print('sections 1-3 match the prototype')
EOF

git status --short -- data storygame packages .plans | grep -v -E 'knowledge.yaml|pacing.yaml|storylet-routes.yaml|storylets.md|world.yaml|story-data-redesign-plan.md|1a-password-officer-plan.md|situation_trace.py' && echo 'FAIL: unexpected changes outside ownership (listed above)' && exit 1
echo CHECK PASSED
exit 0
